Robert Blake is a vibrant 11-16 community where students are known, valued and challenged. Headteacher's Welcome
Welcome to Robert Blake Academy.
At Robert Blake, we believe every young person deserves an education that nurtures both exceptional learning and exceptional character. Our vision, “Excellence in Learning, Strength in Character,” drives everything we do. We are proud to be a school community where students feel a deep sense of ambition, excellence, character, and belonging, as evidenced through our mission statement.
We expect our students to be the very best version of themselves, and we support them every step of the way. Our new SMART values — Self?discipline | Motivation | Aspiration | Respect | Togetherness — shape daily life in school and guide the choices our students make. These values are brought to life through our rich programme of character development, underpinned by core virtues associated with each value.
These virtues help our learners grow into confident, responsible, and compassionate young adults, ready to take their respectful and positive place in society.
Robert Blake is a vibrant 11–16 community where students are known, valued, and challenged. We build strong relationships and a culture of high expectations, ensuring every child feels safe, supported, and motivated to achieve more than they thought possible. Our Pastoral Leaders and Student Services team work closely with families to create a strong sense of belonging from the moment students join us.
We are committed to delivering an engaging, ambitious curriculum, enriched by partnerships with local and regional providers including University Centre Somerset (UCS) College Group, Richard Huish College, neighbouring Sedgemoor Secondary schools and our feeder Primary schools. Students benefit from a wide range of enrichment opportunities across the arts, sport, outdoor learning, and STEM, as well as cultural and academic experiences designed to broaden horizons. Throughout their time at Robert Blake, every student will visit places of cultural, historical, and scientific importance and have opportunities for national and international educational visits.
Student voice is central to our ongoing improvement through our active Prefect team, School Council and regular surveys of students, staff, and parents. We listen carefully and act promptly to make our school even stronger. We are proud of our consistently high rates of progression into further education, apprenticeships, and employment, supported by robust transition programmes with our partner primary schools and post-16 providers.
Every decision we make is rooted in the best interests of our students, academically, socially, and emotionally. Our rewards system celebrates hard work, positive behaviour, attendance, and commitment to learning underpinned by our SMART values. Everywhere you look in our school, you will see us recognising success and sharing achievements.
Robert Blake is an exciting place to learn, grow, and flourish. Our students, staff, and wider community are immensely proud of our school, and I warmly invite you to visit us and experience firsthand the ambition, energy, and excellence that define who we are.
We look forward to welcoming you to our community.

British Values and SMSC
Please see the document below for the full statement about our approach to British Values and SMSC.
We are proud to be a thriving, diverse and caring community at Robert Blake. Whilst we are an inclusive and committed school in ensuring all our students leave with excellent outcomes and a range of skills to be successful in the future, we place an equal emphasis on reaching high levels of values and personal development. We are dedicated in shaping our students to become citizens to be proud of in both a modern Britain and the wider world.
We undertake to do everything that we can to uphold the DfE in their assertion that schools “need to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.” We believe it is important to shape our students to respect these values by ensuring that our curriculum provides enriching, tangible and far-reaching learning experiences. These experiences should encourage our students to make their own decisions, form opinions and challenge perceived boundaries. Therefore, experiences within school which emphasises British values and teaches students to consider Spiritual, Cultural, Social and Moral matters (SMSC) both in the classroom and through wider opportunities are essential.
Through our commitment to promote British values and SMSC we want every child to:
This document provides both a detailed audit and examples of where we are proud that these commitments are met at Robert Blake. These are through a wide range of educational activities and experiences a learner gains at Robert Blake. This may occur due to the delivery of curriculum areas, or in various other settings within the school community. Examples include assemblies, enrichment programmes, work experience, careers guidance, working with Young Carers, Student Councils and Parliament, Prefects, delivery of PSHE via our Confidence for Life Programme, Olympic Day, Sports Leaders, DofE and our House system.

Governors
Function - To determine the strategic policy of Robert Blake and monitor the implementation and success of that policy.
The role of the governing body is also to be a "Critical Friend"; supporting the Principal, staff and school as a whole. The governing body's role is also to question decisions which they either do not fully understand, or may have concerns about.
Composition:
There are 5 members of the Governing Body in 2 categories:
1 Principal
4 Co-opted governors.
Officers:
Finance - Sean Warren

ASN - Sean Warren

Committees:
Once per term we hold the following meetings, all of which are attended by Michelle Dyer and nominated members of SLT:
Additionally, the non staff members of the Governing Body are divided into the Governor First committee and the Appeals committee.
Standing items on all agendas align with Ofsted's Education Inspection Framework (EIF). In addition, policies and new initiatives are scrutinised, discussed and approved while attendance and exclusions are reported. We often have presentations from both Staff and Students to keep governors up to date with the school.
All governors have links to both a department and a school improvement area; these links are carried out individually and in groups. Governors are also expected to undergo mandatory training, such as safeguarding and finance, to enable them to carry out their role to the best of their abilities.
Non-confidential minutes from the meetings are available upon request from the Clerk.

Young Carers
What is a Young Carer?
Newsletter and Communications
Meet the Young Carers Team
Students can be young carers for lots of different reasons and we want to hear from you if you think you are a young carer as there maybe other support we can put in place to help. Here are some examples of some young carer scenarios:
• They might be providing physical support to a parent with a physical illness. They may be cooking, fetching things or helping tasks like putting on shoes or doing the shopping. This might extend to dropping and collecting their siblings to and from school
• They might be helping someone who is disabled with more personal tasks, like getting dressed, bathing or changing
• Or it could be more emotional support, like if their autistic sibling is upset, taking responsibility of young siblings parents are unwell or attending health appointments
• Or checking that a parent/carer with anxiety or depression is OK
Please come to speak to us about this in your own way. If face to face, you can find us in our offices, tell student services, your tutor or a member of staff that you trust. If you are not quite ready to speak to someone then please send us a message on Tootoot.

KS3 ( Year 7, 8 & 9)
Welcome to the Revision Section of Our Robert Blake Website.
Revision is incredibly important for students. Throughout their time at Robert Blake, students will study a huge range of subjects with the vast majority taking 9 GCSEs at the end of Year 11. There is a large amount of knowledge that students will need to be able to recall and apply in each of these subjects, so relying on a single lesson without then revisiting this material will mean that they do not perform to their full potential.
As well as improved exam and assessment outcomes there are many other benefits to revising. Students who revise often are more likely to remember things for longer and therefore will not need to ‘cram’ on the run up to exams. They will have increased confidence and therefore minimise anxiety experienced before sitting exams.
There have been a large number of studies that have been done on revision and though we know that revision is extremely effective at improving outcomes, these studies have also shown that not all techniques are equally effective. Things like re-reading, copying notes or highlighting have been shown to have little impact as revision strategies.
At Robert Blake we teach students how to revise through fortnightly revision curriculum sessions, delivered at tutor time. Through this programme students learn how to revise effectively with a focus on 3 main strategies that have been shown to have great impact:
Flashcards (A self-testing strategy)
Mind Maps (A mapping strategy)

Confidence For Life/PSHE
PSHE and RSE – Curriculum Vision
The delivery of PSHE is known internally as Confidence for Life and is delivered fortnightly to students at Robert Blake Academy. This provision is intended to ensure that students are not only provided with important knowledge, but they also consider and challenge perceptions which are related to character development. Each lesson will underpin particular themes, sometimes focusing on a brand-new topic, but also developing on prior learning which was age appropriate at the time. These are:
In every lesson all students are encouraged to share opinions and discuss topics, being respectful and tolerant to other people’s views. The nature of the content is intended to ensure that students leave the classroom with a sense of identity for their place in the world and a respect of others; developing their understanding of the wider world and to be able to consider the rights and responsibilities of others, who can be active citizens that we can be proud of.
Students are also encouraged to challenge different points of view, breaking down misconceptions that they have about different groups in society, being respectful of protected characteristics. There is also a focus on educating students with regards to being able to consider and look after their wellbeing, to develop character values of being more respectful, kind and responsible individuals.
Whilst statutory content is delivered through confidence for Life lessons, there is also important content regarding RSE delivered via Science, Health and Social Care and IT.
Parents have the right to request that their child be withdrawn from some or all of sex education delivered as part of statutory RSE. However, it is requested that parents and, as appropriate, the child should raise this matter with the Robert Blake Academy to ensure that their wishes are understood and to clarify the nature and purpose of the curriculum. We will document this process to ensure a record is kept.
There are several careers related foci covered in the lessons, especially in KS4, where students prepare for work experience placements, future careers or potential college courses. Information on careers can be found on the following:
Each child’s Unifrog account
